title: Understanding the superconducting proximity effect in semiconductors through quantum oscillations
authors: Milo Coombs, Teun A. J. van Schijndel, Yu Wu, Jason T. Dong, Yilmaz Gul, Julian Choi, Christopher J. Palmstrøm, Greg P. Mazur
abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor hybrids host emergent states of matter and offer a platform for new qubits, but the superconducting metal shunts electrical transport, which rules out conventional semiconductor characterization and leaves the hybrid parameters to speculation. Here we determine density, mass, $g$-factor, mobility and subband occupation beneath the superconductor, from Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations of a buried InAs quantum well under Al, Sn, V, Nb, Ta and Re films, with a Dingle analysis that accounts for the shunt. Every metal adds an interface subband whose occupation falls into one of two classes, whereas the mass and $g$-factor of the buried well are unchanged to within 10\%. Within the uncertainty set by the transport mobility, no film shortens the quantum lifetime of the buried well, and Al and Sn lengthen it. Quantum lifetimes bound the hybridization of the interface subband to 2-4~meV. These measurements supply the normal-state parameters that tunnelling spectroscopy renormalizes but cannot measure.
summary: This work investigates superconducting proximity effects in semiconductor/superconductor hybrids by measuring quantum oscillations in a buried InAs quantum well. By analyzing the SdH oscillations under various superconducting films, the authors determine the intrinsic normal-state parameters of the semiconductor. This technique overcomes the ambiguity caused by the superconducting metal shunt, providing crucial data for understanding interface physics.
main_problem: The primary challenge is accurately characterizing the electronic parameters of a semiconductor quantum well when it is buried beneath a superconducting metal film, as the metal shorts the electrical transport.
main_result: The study successfully determines the normal-state parameters (density, mass, g-factor) of the buried semiconductor using quantum oscillations, showing that the superconducting metal induces a distinct interface subband without altering the core parameters of the well.
method: The analysis relies on measuring Shubnikov-de Haas (SdH) oscillations in the presence of superconducting films, complemented by a Dingle analysis that explicitly accounts for the shunt resistance.
model_or_system: The system is a superconductor-semiconductor hybrid, specifically an InAs quantum well placed beneath various superconducting metals (Al, Sn, Nb, etc.). The physics involves analyzing the superconducting proximity effect and the resulting interface subband formation.
key_observables: Shubnikov-de Haas oscillation frequencies, oscillation amplitudes (analyzed via Dingle fitting), cyclotron masses, and g-factors.
important_parameters: Quantum lifetime ($	au_q$), superconducting gap ($\Delta_0$), quasiparticle weight ($Z$), and the coupling strength ($\Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the SdH oscillations of the buried well remain measurable despite the shunt, and that the measured parameters can be separated from the superconducting renormalization effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the buried well and the metal-induced interface subband, and show the SdH oscillation envelopes for both the fundamental and interface branches fitted using Dingle analysis.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of shunt-induced ambiguity, presents the measurement technique using multiple superconducting films, analyzes the resulting quantum oscillations to extract parameters, and concludes by comparing these findings to predictions from tunneling spectroscopy.
why_interesting: The methodology of using quantum oscillations to probe parameters inaccessible via standard tunneling spectroscopy in superconducting hybrids provides a powerful, complementary diagnostic tool for studying superconducting interfaces and proximity effects.
